passage: At the aangan, Mahima counted loudly at the wall while Nilesh dashed inside. Bhaiya, the older cousin, had won last time by hiding in the big almirah, so Nilesh squeezed in among the folded quilts and pulled the door almost shut. Mahima searched the cot, the kitchen and the storeroom and never thought of the almirah. Nilesh giggled softly. It worked only because Mahima did not know the trick.

qa.a: Nilesh hid in the big almirah among the folded quilts.

qa.q: What was Nilesh feeling inside the almirah?
qa.a: Nilesh was excited and pleased with the plan, which is why Nilesh giggled softly while Mahima searched.

qa.q: What alternative could Nilesh use next round, and why?
qa.a: Nilesh could try a different spot from Bhaiya's, because Mahima may learn about the almirah and a copied trick only works while the seeker is unaware.

qa.q: How does Mahima see the game after Nilesh's win?
qa.a: Mahima searched the cot, kitchen and storeroom and may feel puzzled about where Nilesh went, and may look in the almirah the next time.

grounding: A child hides in the almirah because an older cousin won there last time, and it works only because the seeker does not know the trick.

passage: Last summer in Seville, cousin Ulla had won hide-and-seek by squeezing into Grandma's big wardrobe. This year Pablo remembered. When his friend Mateo began counting, Pablo ran straight to the wardrobe, pulled the door almost shut and crouched among the coats. Mateo, who hadn't been there last summer, searched the kitchen and the garden. Ulla walked past and winked. Pablo stayed hidden until Mateo gave up.

qa.a: He crouched among the coats in the wardrobe.

qa.q: What was Pablo feeling as he stayed hidden?
qa.a: He was probably excited and pleased that Ulla's trick was working for him.

qa.q: What else could Pablo try when playing with Ulla?
qa.a: He would need a new spot, because Ulla knows the wardrobe trick and would look there first.

qa.q: How does the wardrobe trick look to Ulla?
qa.a: Ulla recognises her own trick and is amused, winking because she knows Mateo won't guess.

grounding: A child hides in the wardrobe because an older cousin won there before, and it works only because the seeker doesn't know the trick.

passage: In the community centre crèche, the steel almirah held the nap mats. Last week Wasim's cousin Naveen had won by hiding inside it. Today the new helper, Kiran didi, was seeking. Wasim tiptoed in and crouched on the mats, leaving the door open a crack. Kiran didi checked under tables, behind the curtain. She never looked in the almirah. Naveen, sitting out, smirked. Wasim giggled into his knees.

qa.q: What did the steel almirah hold?
What was Wasim feeling as he giggled into his knees?
qa.a: He was excited and pleased to be copying Naveen's winning spot.

qa.q: What else could Wasim try if Naveen were seeking?
qa.a: He would need a new spot, because Naveen knows the almirah trick and would look there straight away.

qa.q: How does Naveen see Wasim's hiding place?
qa.a: Naveen knows the trick is his own and finds it funny that the new helper doesn't know it.

grounding: A child hides in the almirah because his cousin won there before, and it works only because the new seeker doesn't know the trick.
